# 05. UI

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Set the visual and interaction quality bar for polished, responsive, accessible static websites.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A responsive layout standard for mobile, tablet, laptop, desktop, wide desktop, and browser zoom.
- [ ] A component inventory for navigation, buttons, links, cards, forms, accordions, tabs, alerts, tables, media, galleries, and footers.
- [ ] A color role system covering canvas, surface, text, muted text, border, focus, action, success, warning, error, and brand accents.
- [ ] A typography scale with headings, body text, captions, labels, quotes, code, navigation, and form text.
- [ ] A spacing scale and layout grid that remain readable without fixed viewport-width font scaling.
- [ ] A UI state matrix for default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, selected, expanded, loading, success, and error.
- [ ] An icon policy using open-source icons, accessible labels, consistent stroke, and no icon-only controls without names.
- [ ] A visual QA reference with approved screenshots for key templates and breakpoints.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Text must never overlap, clip, or become unreadable at supported viewport widths and common zoom levels.
- [ ] Interactive elements must look interactive and must have visible focus states.
- [ ] Buttons, links, and navigation items must be visually distinct by role and importance.
- [ ] Cards must be used for repeated items or framed tools, not as a default wrapper for every section.
- [ ] Hero-scale type must be reserved for true hero contexts, not compact cards or sidebars.
- [ ] Color must not be the only indicator of status, selection, errors, required fields, or active navigation.
- [ ] UI density must match the website type: service and business sites should prioritize scanability and decision support.
- [ ] Visual polish must survive real content lengths, translated text, missing images, long names, and validation errors.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check contrast for all text, icons, borders needed for understanding, focus rings, and disabled states.
- [ ] Check line length, line height, paragraph spacing, heading hierarchy, and text wrap on every template.
- [ ] Check that media crops preserve important subjects and do not obscure text.
- [ ] Check that menus, drawers, modals, and sticky elements do not cover content at mobile heights.
- [ ] Check that the UI works without hover and with coarse pointers.
- [ ] Check that long CTAs and translated labels fit without layout breakage.
- [ ] Check that browser default styles are reset only where replacement accessible styles exist.
- [ ] Check that print styles are acceptable for pages users may save or print.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid one-note palettes dominated by a single hue family unless the brand explicitly requires it and contrast remains strong.
- [ ] Avoid negative letter spacing, viewport-based font scaling, and fragile absolute positioning for text.
- [ ] Avoid decorative gradients, blobs, or overlays that reduce readability or performance.
- [ ] Avoid carousels for critical content unless the content is also available in static form.
- [ ] Avoid using placeholder imagery or lorem ipsum in production screenshots.
- [ ] Avoid hover-only labels for essential controls.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The interface must look designed with real content, not only with ideal mockup copy.
- [ ] Every component must align to the same spacing, type, color, and state logic.
- [ ] The page must remain visually stable during loading, font swap, image load, and interaction.
- [ ] The UI must be restrained enough that content and action remain the focus.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script to flag missing image dimensions, missing focus-support CSS, oversized assets, and missing viewport metadata.
- [ ] Use screenshot comparison with free tools such as Playwright when visual regression coverage is needed.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Visual hierarchy: dominant primary message, clear heading scale, distinct CTAs, controlled spacing, clear relationships between cards/images/icons/text, and no competing focal points.
- [ ] Layout QA: consistent grids, precise alignment, controlled content width, readable line length, purposeful images, stable card proportions, varied but coherent sections, and clean responsive behavior.
- [ ] Typography QA: fonts load, sizes and weights are readable, line height is comfortable, text wraps cleanly, links are identifiable, captions/labels/errors are legible, and mobile text remains readable.
- [ ] Color and contrast: brand and accent colors are consistent, focus/success/error/disabled states are clear, light and dark sections are readable, and color is not the only source of meaning.
- [ ] UI polish: buttons, icons, cards, images, borders, radius, shadows, dividers, overlays, animations, hover effects, and mobile spacing feel intentional and production-ready.
- [ ] Premium quality: the first impression feels intentional, refined, trustworthy, not template-like, not one-note, not cluttered, and not unfinished on any page.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
